data.why: The repository ships no local MEI files to open (its own sample list is a CSV of remote GitHub URLs), so synthetic MEI files were written matching the record's described test cases: a clean baseline and a file with an invalid pname='h', a note missing its dur attribute, and a measure with 5 beats encoded in a 4/4 meter.

goals: Open a digitized or converted music encoding (MEI/MusicXML/Humdrum) and view it rendered as music notation alongside its underlying markup
Validate the encoding against the MEI schema and locate each reported error in both the text and the rendered score
Correct encoding errors (wrong pitch names, missing duration attributes, incorrect beat counts) in the code pane and confirm the fix via re-validation and re-rendering
Navigate between the rendered score and the markup by clicking notes or measures to inspect and edit specific elements
Play back the corrected encoding via MIDI to confirm it sounds as intended
Export the cleaned-up encoding as MEI, MIDI, or SVG for downstream use

review.summary: The tree matches mei-friend's stated purpose, cleaning up OMR or converted MEI, with sensible load/find/correct/export phases, and most cited screens show exactly the edit claimed. Before filing, it needs the export evidence replaced (029/030 only show the playback bar), schema validation, playback and editorial markup added as tasks, the broken metcon findings stated, and f6 linked to the right task.
